questions.question: Which observation describes pharmacodynamics rather than pharmacokinetics?

choices.text: A medication blocks a receptor, preventing another substance from activating it
A medication is absorbed through nasal mucosa into the bloodstream
A medication is removed from the body through elimination
Reduced tissue blood flow delays a medication’s absorption

questions.explanation: Pharmacodynamics describes medication actions on the body, such as receptor blockade. Absorption and elimination describe the body’s handling of the medication.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Absorption describes how medication enters the bloodstream.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Elimination describes removal from the body.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: A change in absorption is a pharmacokinetic issue.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: An agonist activates a receptor.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Elimination removes a drug from the body rather than blocking its receptor effect.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Absorption describes entry into the bloodstream.

questions.question: A medication is given at 14:00. Improvement first appears at 14:03 and is greatest at 14:10. What do these observations identify?

choices.text: Onset at 3 minutes; peak at 10 minutes
Peak at 3 minutes; onset at 10 minutes
Duration of 3 minutes; elimination at 10 minutes
Onset at 10 minutes; duration of 7 minutes

questions.explanation: Onset is the interval until effects begin; peak is when the maximum clinical effect occurs.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: This reverses the terms.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The end of effects and removal from the body are not established.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: The first effects occur at 3 minutes; duration cannot be determined without the end of effects.

The interval from administration to the first clinical effect
The time at which its clinical effect is strongest
The amount administered to produce the desired effect

questions.explanation: Duration describes how long clinical effects last.

questions.question: Which comparison correctly distinguishes unintended from untoward medication effects?

choices.text: Unintended: undesirable with little risk; untoward: potentially harmful
Unintended: desired clinical response; untoward: potentially harmful
Unintended: potentially harmful; untoward: undesirable with little risk
Unintended: undesirable with little risk; untoward: delayed therapeutic onset

questions.explanation: The distinction concerns the risk of undesired effects, not whether a drug is effective.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: A desired response is a therapeutic effect.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The risk descriptions are reversed.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Untoward describes harm, not the time to onset.

Inhibition of platelet aggregation; suspected cardiac chest pain
Aspirin allergy; inhibition of platelet aggregation

questions.question: A patient in shock responds more slowly than expected to a medication delivered into tissue. Which explanation is consistent with altered pharmacokinetics?

choices.text: Reduced tissue blood flow can delay absorption and delivery
Shock guarantees more rapid absorption from every tissue
Slow onset establishes that the medication was an antagonist
A delayed response proves that the medication had no indication

questions.explanation: Shock and route can affect absorption and delivery; response timing alone does not establish mechanism or appropriateness.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Reduced perfusion can impair rather than accelerate uptake.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Receptor mechanism cannot be inferred from onset alone.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: A valid indication can exist despite delayed response.

questions.question: A patient has suspected cardiac chest pain and a documented severe allergy to aspirin. How should the allergy affect aspirin administration?

choices.text: It is a contraindication even though the complaint otherwise supports aspirin
It is a relative concern that the chest-pain indication automatically outweighs
It is a reason to reduce the dose while keeping the oral route
It matters only if a reaction occurs after administration

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: The indication does not automatically override this allergy.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: A lower dose does not remove the allergy risk.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: The known allergy must be considered before administration.

questions.question: What distinguishes a relative contraindication from an absolute one?

choices.text: Potential benefits may outweigh the risk, requiring appropriate clinical direction
The medication has no risk and requires no further evaluation
The medication must never be given under any circumstance
It is simply another name for a medication’s indication

questions.explanation: A relative contraindication requires risk-benefit consideration rather than an unconditional prohibition.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: There is a risk to weigh.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: That describes an absolute contraindication.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: An indication describes why a medication may help, not its risk.

questions.question: A patient’s complaint matches an indication for a medication. What still needs to be established before administration?

choices.text: That contraindications are absent and all required safety checks and authorization are satisfied
That the indication is present, then treat the complaint without further medication checks
That the drug produced benefit in another patient with a similar complaint
That the medication’s trade name sounds appropriate for the symptom

questions.explanation: An indication is necessary but does not complete assessment of safety, dose, route, or authorization.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: The same patient can have both an indication and a contraindication.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Another patient’s response cannot replace individual checks.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: A name alone does not establish appropriateness.

archivedQuestions.question: The length of time a medication’s clinical effects persist is its _____.
archivedQuestions.explanation: Duration describes how long clinical effects last.

choices.text: duration
onset

incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Elimination describes removal of the medication from the body.
